title: Finite generator master equations and uniformization

items.title: Finite column generator
items.statement: Define the column convention for a finite generator Q: off-diagonal entries are nonnegative, each column sums to zero, and q_ij is the rate from source j to destination i.
items.strategy: State the finite state set, sign convention, column-sum condition, exit rates, and normalized column probability vectors.

sources.title: Ward Whitt, Continuous-Time Markov Chains, full lecture notes (2006)
sources.locator: §§3.1–3.2, PDF pp. 6–9; transpose the notes' row-vector convention to this page's stated column convention.

sources.locator: §II, equations (2.4)–(2.6), printed pp. 044104-2–044104-3; column probability vector and column-sum-zero reaction matrix.

items.title: Finite matrix exponential series and its identities
items.statement: For a finite real matrix A, its factorial power series converges locally uniformly, differentiates to A exp(tA), and satisfies exp(A)exp(B)=exp(A+B) when A and B commute.
items.strategy: Use an induced matrix norm to dominate the series and difference quotients, then regroup the absolutely convergent double series by total degree.

sources.title: Ward Whitt, Continuous-Time Markov Chains, full lecture notes (2006)
sources.locator: §3.2, Theorem 3.2 and its proof, PDF pp. 8–10; finite matrix exponential representation and its ODE.

sources.locator: §II, equation (2.6), printed pp. 044104-2–044104-3; finite-dimensional solution by exp(At).

items.title: A geometric upper bound for a Poisson right tail
items.statement: For N distributed as Pois(mu), mu>0, and integer K>=0 with mu<K+2, bound P(N>K) by the first omitted Poisson mass divided by 1-mu/(K+2).
items.strategy: Bound each successive omitted mass by a geometric ratio using the exact Poisson mass recurrence.

sources.title: Bennett L. Fox and Peter W. Glynn, Computing Poisson Probabilities
sources.locator: §§1–6, printed pp. 440–445; recursive Poisson weights, rigorously bounded truncation tails, and warnings against estimating omitted mass by rounded subtraction.

items.title: Given countable nonexplosive pure-jump chain with finite rates
items.statement: Define the countable-state, time-homogeneous pure-jump Markov chain input, its finite exit rates and transition-rate convention, and state nonexplosion as an explicit hypothesis rather than a conclusion.
items.strategy: Specify the state space, off-diagonal rates, holding and destination laws, Markov property, path convention, and nonexplosion condition.

sources.title: Ward Whitt, Continuous-Time Markov Chains, full lecture notes (2006)
sources.locator: §§2–3, printed pp. 2–15; transition kernels, holding times, transition rates, and the finite-state restriction used in the matrix ODE argument.

items.title: Countable-state l1 distance for mass functions
items.statement: Define the l1 distance between nonnegative summable mass functions on a countable state space as the countable sum of absolute coordinate differences; it is finite for a probability mass and a subprobability mass.
items.strategy: Give the nonnegative-series convention and the finite upper bound by the sum of the two total masses.

sources.title: Brian Munsky and Mustafa Khammash, The Finite State Projection Algorithm for the Solution of the Chemical Master Equation
sources.locator: §II, Theorem 2.2 and equation (2.8), printed p. 044104-4; componentwise truncation error and missing-mass certificate.

items.title: The finite uniformized matrix is column stochastic
items.statement: If nu>=max_j(-Q_jj)>0 for a finite column generator Q, then P=I+Q/nu has nonnegative entries and every column sums to one; if nu=0, Q=0.
items.strategy: Check off-diagonal, diagonal, and column-sum conditions directly; handle the zero-rate case separately.

sources.title: Ward Whitt, Continuous-Time Markov Chains, full lecture notes (2006)
sources.locator: §3.4, equations (3.24)–(3.27), PDF pp. 14–15; transpose the row-stochastic matrix to the column convention used here.

items.title: Killed finite-state projection and cemetery lift
items.statement: For a given countable chain and finite nonempty F, define first-exit killing, the principal killed subgenerator, and the conservative finite generator obtained by appending an absorbing cemetery state.
items.strategy: Define the first exit time, initial mass transfer to the cemetery state, and exact finite rate matrix under the column convention.

items.title: Finite master equation and uniformization formula
items.statement: The unique solution of p'=Qp with probability initial vector p0 is exp(tQ)p0 and, for any admissible nu>0, the Poisson-weighted series of P^k p0; nu=0 gives p0.
items.strategy: Identify the Poisson mixture with the matrix exponential, differentiate the locally convergent series, prove uniqueness by multiplying by exp(-tQ), and handle Q=0.

items.title: Budgeted uniformization accumulation with time splitting
items.statement: Return a nonnegative finite Poisson-series approximation or an explicit budget/certificate-unavailable status, using substeps with Poisson parameter at most one and a certified geometric right-tail bound. Split nu*t into finitely many means at most one, choose a finite-budget truncation, and return an outward-certified Poisson-tail bound plus a separately certified l1 vector-arithmetic error. Rounded executions must certify scalar control/tail decisions as well as vector error; uncertain decisions return certificate-unavailable.
items.strategy: Split nu*t into finitely many means at most one, choose the least tail-certified truncation within the total term budget, and apply matrix-free P actions and Poisson recurrences.

sources.locator: §§1–3, printed pp. 440–443; stable recursive Poisson weights, finite truncation, and avoidance of rounded complementary-mass subtraction.

items.title: Uniformization truncation, mass loss, and arithmetic-error ledger
items.statement: Exact partial sums are nonnegative and substochastic; their one-series omitted l1 mass equals the Poisson tail, and time-split transient error is bounded by certified Poisson-tail upper bounds plus separately certified arithmetic/algebraic vector error.
items.strategy: Use stochastic column sums to compute exact missing mass, a telescoping difference of stochastic and substochastic operators for time-split truncation, and the triangle inequality for a certified execution error.

items.title: Finite-state killed projection has an exact lost-mass certificate
items.statement: For a given nonexplosive countable chain, the cemetery lift records first-exit probability; the killed vector is componentwise below the full marginal, its embedded l1 error equals lost mass, and bounded-observable error is at most half the observable oscillation times lost mass.
items.strategy: Derive the finite cemetery generator from first-jump rates, identify its solution using the finite master equation, then compare pathwise the killed and full distributions.

items.title: Finite-budget adaptive finite-state projection
items.statement: Try only a supplied finite nested list of finite projections, record a certified lost-mass interval for each completed solve, and return certified or inconclusive without claiming that a sufficient finite projection exists.
items.strategy: For each finite candidate, solve its cemetery lift with the budgeted uniformization routine, form an outward-certified lost-mass interval, and stop at the first upper bound within tolerance or at a finite failure/budget boundary.

sources.title: Brian Munsky and Mustafa Khammash, The Finite State Projection Algorithm for the Solution of the Chemical Master Equation
sources.locator: §III, finite-state projection algorithm, printed pp. 044104-4–044104-5; each enlargement is checked by its computed mass certificate.

items.title: Adaptive projection certificates are sound and finite-budgeted
items.statement: The adaptive algorithm terminates after at most its declared number of projections and can return certified only when a validated upper endpoint proves the actual lost mass, hence the l1 and bounded-observable errors, are within tolerance; inconclusive makes no existence claim.
items.strategy: Use the finite loop bound for termination and the projection loss theorem plus interval containment for the certified branch.

title: Finite generator master equations and uniformization — Examples

items.title: Two-state gating through uniformization
items.statement: For a two-state off/on gate with rates alpha and beta, compute the column generator, uniformization matrix, and transient on probability from the off state.
items.strategy: Solve the scalar master equation and identify its solution with the Poisson mixture from the finite uniformization theorem.

sources.title: Ward Whitt, Continuous-Time Markov Chains, full lecture notes (2006)
sources.locator: §3.2 and §3.4, PDF pp. 7–16; finite generator and uniformization formula.

items.title: Three-state birth-death chain with a certified Poisson tail
items.statement: For a specified three-state birth-death generator, compute P^k p0 through k=4 and the exact truncated mass at nu*t=1, then certify the omitted tail with the geometric bound.
items.strategy: Multiply the explicit column-stochastic matrix four times and use exact Poisson weights and the local geometric tail theorem.

sources.title: Bennett L. Fox and Peter W. Glynn, Computing Poisson Probabilities
sources.locator: Proposition 1 and §§1–3, printed pp. 440–443; truncated Poisson-weight calculations and certified omitted mass.

items.title: Immigration-death chain projected onto two states
items.statement: For unit immigration and linear death rates, verify nonexplosion by the declared Lyapunov supplier and compute the cemetery mass for F={0,1}, noting that the full chain can return to F after first exit.
items.strategy: Check the reaction-network Lyapunov inequality, form the three-state cemetery generator, solve its finite ODE, and identify its cemetery coordinate with first-exit loss.

sources.title: Brian Munsky and Mustafa Khammash, The Finite State Projection Algorithm for the Solution of the Chemical Master Equation
sources.locator: §II Theorem 2.2 and §III, printed pp. 044104-4–044104-5; finite projection and cemetery/lost-mass certificate.

items.title: Equal mean trajectories do not determine a master-equation state
items.statement: Two distinct finite generators with the same initial law give the same constant mean trajectory but different full probability vectors.
items.strategy: Solve both finite master equations, compare their first moments, and exhibit a differing coordinate for every positive time.
